reviews.text:
It's been a long time since I stopped by, but the neat and clean taste is still the same.
This house is a modern interpretation of sundae, and the restaurant environment has completely changed the image of existing sundae soup restaurants.
It's a far cry from the Sundae Guk restaurant, which has a neat and clean store environment but has foul smells and an unhygienic environment.
Just like the image of the restaurant, the taste of the sundae soup is very neat and clean without any unpleasant smells.
This restaurant's specialty, sundae steak, grilled on an iron plate reminiscent of German homemade sausages, is also unique and delicious.
In addition to meat, the sundae is filled with various ingredients such as black glutinous rice, bean sprouts, and carrots, so it has a good chewy texture and the taste harmony is excellent without any overpowering taste.
If you like sundae, this is a restaurant I highly recommend.

reviews.text:
Hyehwa Alley Naengmyeon is located about a 7-minute walk from Exit 4 of Hyehwa Station on Subway Line 4.
In addition, there is a bus stop near the store where various city buses passing through Gangbuk, Gangnam, and Gangdong pass, making public transportation very convenient.

The area around the store is near Sungkyunkwan University and Catholic University, so various theaters, restaurants, and cafes are concentrated in the vibrant atmosphere unique to Daehakro.
It is a popular place for outings or meetings with friends, lovers, and family before or after a meal.

It is located between Daehak-ro, where Sungkyunkwan University and Sookmyung Women’s University are located, and Exit 1 of Hyehwa Station, famous for its theater district.
It's great for meeting friends before or after a meal, a date with a lover, or an outing with family.

There is no separate parking space in the store building, so we recommend using the nearby Bulgama parking lot or public parking lot.

For reference, the Bulgama parking lot is for 30-60 minutes (KRW 5,000) and 1 hour and 20 minutes (KRW 1,000).

The store has the appearance of a traditional alley store, with a simple design that gives a familiar yet warm feeling.

The store's sign is black letters on a white background and is small enough to create a cute alley atmosphere.
It was easy to see at a glance even from a distance.

The store entrance has a clean and simple style, allowing first-time visitors to access it comfortably.

At the entrance to the store, small picture frames and props create a cute and cozy atmosphere that matches the atmosphere of a restaurant in a small alley.

Before entering the entrance, the Hyehwa Alley Naengmyeon menu and prices are written down to help first-time visitors easily check the menu and make a choice.

When you enter the store, the phrase “Nice to meet you” written in cute font is quite cute and cozy.

The interior of the store is a combination of white and wood tones, creating a warm and comfortable atmosphere.
In addition, the soft lighting, picture frames on the walls, and various props give the restaurant a cozy feel that is unique to alley restaurants.

Although the store space is small, the tables are arranged efficiently and can accommodate a variety of visitors, from one visitor to four visitors.
Tables are spaced at an appropriate distance without causing discomfort due to the conversation or eye contact of people next to you.

Some seats are in the form of bar tables, making it convenient for dining alone.

On one wall, there are photos and explanations showing the history of Hyehwa Alley Naengmyeon.
In Hyehwa, you can feel how much the store is a popular attraction loved by local residents.

Customers can freely use water, bone broth, and cups of water on their own.

Everything from the sterilizing dryer that stores cups to the water purifier and bone broth container is managed neatly.

There is an apron behind the water purifier, and you can bring the amount of apron you need.

There is a store order kiosk above the table, so you can view the store menu and prices and even place an order at once.

Basically, there is a neat cutlery container containing spoons, chopsticks, and forks, and like a cold noodle restaurant, vinegar and mustard are placed on each table.

The store menu offers a variety of menu items at reasonable prices.

The store's signature dish, pollack raw noodles, can be enjoyed for 11,000 won. It contains fresh pollack raw fish and cool cold noodle broth, so customers are highly satisfied.
Mul naengmyeon and bibim naengmyeon are 8,000 won and 9,000 won, respectively, so you can enjoy cool and refreshing naengmyeon at a reasonable price.

A cold pork set that allows you to eat cold noodles and pork cutlet together is 13,000 won, and a combination of cold noodles and grilled bulgogi is 14,000 won.

In addition, there are various options at reasonable prices, such as sirloin pork cutlet at 10,000 won, bibimbap at 9,000 won, and stone pot bibimbap at 10,000 won.

reviews.text:
These days, the price of pork belly has become so expensive that you have to pay at least 8,000 won for 100g to eat delicious pork belly.
Bangmok opened about 3 years ago, and I only passed by it until then. Last time I visited Bangmok 2nd branch, I tried Gabri and Jeongjeongsal and fell in love with it, so I wanted to eat at Bangmok 1st branch, but there was always a wait, so I passed it by, but yesterday I made up my mind and visited early.
There are about 7-8 tables, but it is very cramped. You must take this into account.
I ordered 600g of pork belly and pork neck, 36,000 won. The price is 6,000 won for 100g, which is a really good price.
After waiting for a while, the basic side dishes and sauces were set, hot charcoal fire was brought out, the grill was placed, and then a thick hunk of pork neck and pork belly were served.
Charcoal grill at this price!!!
The staff takes care of all the baking process from beginning to eating, so it is best not to touch the food. The staff were so friendly that it made me feel better.
Turn the meat over, and when the outside is crispy, place the aged paper in the lid of the bowl on the charcoal fire and place the cooked meat on top of the kimchi to begin eating.
When I first tasted the raw meat, it was so tender and seasoned that it was really delicious even when I just ate it. Even compared to the taste of expensive pork belly restaurants, I actually liked it better.
You can eat lettuce with boiled fish in salted fish sauce and eat it with Cheongyang pepper, you can eat it with Myeongnamul with wasabi, or you can just eat it with soy sauce onions and ripe kimchi.
As I was eating the meat for a while, he offered me a big bowl full of kimchi rolled noodles with plenty of seaweed and kimchi. The sour kimchi and the sweet yet savory broth cut out the greasiness of the meat, so we enjoyed it until we both ate all 600g.
I feel blessed to have a restaurant like this nearby.
Next week, I will go to the second branch to eat Hangjeong and Gaburi.

reviews.text: This is a regular restaurant that I have been to more than 10 times. I lost a regular customer today. I ordered radish noodles, but you know that kimchi that is full of white mold and looks like food waste? It smelled like that before I mixed it, so I ate it, but the taste was really disgusting. I came here often and the owner was kind, so I thought about whether or not to tell him, but I thought it would be a bit weird if he sold it to other customers, so I told him that it tasted really weird. But he said, ‘It doesn’t seem to suit your taste.’ We still thought to ourselves, “Oh, that’s a bit weird,” so we ordered extra food because we couldn’t eat that, so we paid for all three items and left. When I came out and asked for a receipt, the first thing I did was ask, ‘Why? He said, ''Do you want to write a review?'' and my partner didn't want to argue, so I said, ''Please give me the receipt.'' two more times, but he first pointed the finger and said, ''I sold it yesterday and the day before that, but the other customers didn't say anything.'' And then my companion got angry and said, ''Is it the customer's fault for saying it tastes strange?'' He raised his voice and said that, so I went in, stopped him, and took him out. As he was leaving, he said again sarcastically, saying, ‘Yes, take it with you.’ I am a service industry worker. I have seen the truth a lot and am trying to understand the customer's perspective. But are you being so aggressive towards the customer because we asked for a receipt, not because we didn't pay or that we would guide you? Regardless of the taste, I'm so disappointed that I felt like they were really friendly up until now. I won't go again, but I think selling food like that with that attitude really doesn't fit the service industry. People will come anyway and people who won't will not come, but you can't run a business for long with that kind of mindset.

reviews.author: Bungeoppang Boy (Bunggeoppang Boy)
reviews.text:
Located about 10 minutes away from Hansung University Entrance Station. It's not hard to find. I visited about 2 years ago and this time I visited again, and I felt like it was certified as a good restaurant just by maintaining the same appearance without much change.

The inside of the restaurant is large and comfortable by my standards. There is some space between the seats and there are additional seats inside. Because of the slightly open kitchen, the noise made while working was a bit loud, but it didn't feel that uncomfortable.

I ordered water makguksu, makguksu, and garlic bossam, and the food came out quickly. It was my first time eating garlic bossam. The sweet garlic on top whetted my appetite and went well with the bossam that came with it. The lean meat was soft and had no unpleasant odor, so it was very delicious to eat, and the combination of dried radish and cabbage that came with it didn't need any explanation.

Makguksu also had a good balance of flavors. The seasoning wasn't too strong or spicy, but the seasoning was just right, and the unique Makguksu noodles had a nice chewy texture. It seemed like you could adjust the spiciness of the seasoning to some extent if you asked for it, and it wasn't too even for my spicy taste buds, so it was a seasoning that anyone could enjoy.

Overall, the food seemed to go well together. They also sell other foods, so you don't have to eat only Makguksu, but if you ever visit, I definitely recommend Makguksu. Seeing as I didn't really think about the price after eating it, it seems like I had a delicious meal. Highly recommended.

reviews.author: kiup kim
reviews.text:
Perhaps because it was raining, the weather, and my heart felt empty, I thought of udon.
My favorite udon restaurant was far away and difficult to find, so I searched Daehakro and found Kenroku Udon Restaurant.
I remember eating there once in Daejeon 3-4 years ago, so I went there.

First of all, it is a store run by the owner alone.
It is self-managed from ordering to receiving food and leaving.
It was a small shop with about 5 to 6 tables inside.

I liked that if you order one per person, you can add additional quantities from regular to triple or triple for free.
First of all, the broth is a bit strong.
Maybe it's because the concept is because it's udon from the Kyushu region.
It was thicker and had a stronger peppery flavor than the Tau Dong restaurant.
Even after drinking water at the store, the taste of pepper remained on my tongue. ^^
Although it was machine-made noodles and not handmade, it still had a chewy texture, but I felt a little disappointed.
Tofu sushi is just tofu with white rice...ㅡㅡ
I think nutritious rice would be better.

Considering the cost-effectiveness, it is a good udon restaurant.
The portions are plentiful and delicious (about three and a half stars).
If you like strong broth, this is a good place.

And the characteristic is that it emphasizes the fiery taste, but in fact, the fiery taste is not felt that well. There is a lot of udon noodles and a lot of broth, but only the roasted green onions have a unique scent, so it has a lot of flavor.

Rather, the pepper taste is really strong. In fact, there are some acquaintances who don't like it that much.

I don't think it's a place you would come and eat. If you want to eat a lot of udon while working nearby, it's not a bad idea to go there. (During weekday lunch, tofu sushi or nutritious rice are also provided free of charge.)

reviews.author: Seohyun Park
reviews.text: This is a delicious steamed kaisendong restaurant I found in Daehakro! First of all, the floral murals on the outside were so pretty that I was entranced, but the interior was also wide-open, so it had an open feel and was really comfortable. I had the Haehwa Gaeban special Kaisendon set and the freshness of the seafood was amazing. The tuna melts in your mouth and the sweet shrimp is really sweet, like it's sprinkled with sugar. The portion is generous, but the ochazuke made with furikake and broth at the end is a real delicacy. I was very satisfied because it was warm and finished cleanly. Ordering via tablet is convenient and the staff are friendly. If you participate in the Naver/SNS review event, you will receive a drink, so make sure to bring it with you. Recommended for those looking for a Hyehwa Station date course or a neat place to eat alone! I intend to visit again.

reviews.author: Choji consistent local guidek
reviews.text: It's been a while since the menu in Google Maps was updated. Now, pork cutlet is 10,000 won and katsudon is 10,000 won... I was surprised to see the price after just looking at the picture. I ordered katsudon, and it seemed like they used good meat, but it was a bit overcooked. I understand it's because people complain if it's undercooked, but there's nothing juicy about it. Katsudon is a style where you put egg sauce on top of pork cutlet, but here it is served separately. I think this is good for bringing out the texture of pork cutlet. The sauce and rice are ok, but the soup and pickles that come on the side are not that great. If it were about 8,000 won overall, it could be said to be value for money, but there are too many options for 10,000 won. It's very disappointing considering the price.

reviews.author: Childcare Assistant TV
reviews.text: I ordered cheese pork cutlet and it felt like the cheese was melting in my mouth. However, the spicy tomato sauce that came with it went well with the pork cutlet. The outside was fried so crispy that I thought it would have been more delicious if I had ordered a regular pork cutlet.

reviews.author: Shin Hye-sun
reviews.text: The pork cutlet was thick and the food was served, but it felt plentiful. I entered by chance, but it was delicious and clean. The restaurant was clean, I thought it had just opened. The owner and staff were friendly, but the only problem was the bathroom... I don't recommend using the bathroom, but I highly recommend it to those who only want to eat.

reviews.author: Jance Journey
reviews.text: The batter is crispy and delicious. The entire menu is 6,500 won, so it's great value for money. However, I wish I could eat it with the sauce separately. It's at the entrance to Naksan Park.

reviews.author: Dangerous Gourmet (Dangerous Gourmet)
reviews.text: I stopped by near Hyehwa Station because I heard there was a menu with all items at the same price. I don't know how the other menus tasted, but what I ate felt like eating kimchi soup and pork cutlet... I wasn't particularly moved and was disappointed. Moreover, it would have been nice to be able to feel the crispiness of the pork cutlet, but perhaps it was a mistake by the staff, and all the pork cutlet came out with a plop in it. That's why I ate soggy pork cutlet. However, the thickness and quality of the meat looks good, so I would like to try other menu items.
